title: Socratic cross-examination with enforced response obligations
question_or_target: Implement tools/council/protocol/socratic.py so a directed question creates a tracked obligation the addressee must discharge within N turns. Falsifiable question: can a participant discharge an obligation with a non-answer, and does the tracker detect evasion rather than counting any reply as a response?
falsifiable_answer: No: a non-answer, including a multi-kilobyte stall, leaves the obligation OPEN. Discharge requires classify_reply to return ANSWER. naive_any_bytes_discharge is kept as the defeated control.
output_schema: command-center/schema/receipt.schema.json profile=council-protocol-module (required: unit_id, artifact_paths[], spec_anchor, evidence[], test_ids[], negative_control_ids[], reviewer_verdict, residual_unknowns[])

reviewer.starts_from: tests and labelled corpus, not the author's summary

negative_controls.description: A 4kB stall reply must remain OPEN, proving the tracker is not counting bytes.
naive_any_bytes_discharge returns true on the same stall the live tracker keeps OPEN.

evidence.claim: The live ledger records OPEN/DISCHARGED/EXPIRED/ESCALATED with per-turn ages.
A labelled evasion corpus is scored by classify_reply; the discrimination rate is reported.

residual_unknowns.claim: tools/council/kernel.py (IMP-0264) is not on this worktree; socratic.py carries its own turn index until the kernel lands.
residual_unknowns.settling_experiment: Re-run probe1 after IMP-0264 with record_turn driven by the kernel event loop rather than the protocol clock.

residual_unknowns.claim: tools/council/integrity/coi.py (IMP-0277) is not on this worktree; seat incompatibility is not enforced here.
residual_unknowns.settling_experiment: Wire ask() through the COI checker once present.

residual_unknowns.claim: Synonym-only answers with no shared content token and no typed cue can still be labelled EVASION (false negative).
residual_unknowns.settling_experiment: Add a labelled synonym slice and report the drop in recall.
